Books I read

What's on my shelf

Books that changed how I think — and the one clear lesson each one left me with.

Small daily attitude choices shape your results more than talent or luck.

Clarity comes from simple frameworks and ruthless prioritisation, not complexity.

What feels like a wall is usually your own self-sabotage — self-awareness is how you climb it.

Reading people is about observing behaviour and context, not guessing minds.

Success feels empty without anchors for the heart — balance all four wheels of life.

What you focus on expands — attention shapes your experience of reality.

Your dominant thoughts and feelings attract your reality — feeling good is a compass.

Live with intention — service, gratitude and small daily heroics are the point.

People respond to genuine interest and appreciation, never criticism.

Worry shrinks when you break problems into actions and live one day at a time.

Burning desire, a definite plan and persistence compound into lasting wealth.

True wealth is time, social, mental, physical and financial — optimise all five.

Purpose lives where what you love, what you're good at and what the world needs overlap.
